rule.description: A method of the maintenance scheduler 'sc' class (struct sc and its sc_ method family, defined in sophia/scheduler/*.c) is flagged when it is oversized for dispatch purposes (clang-tidy readability-function-size, StatementThreshold=23) and its parameter interface is compiler-verified to bind a foreign engine record family (index si*/siplan*, version sv*, wal sw*, page format sd*, format sf*, object so*, environment se*, repository sy*, transaction sx*). Scheduler satellites (scdb, sctask, scworker, scworkerpool, scconf, scprofiler), runtime (sr*) and std (ss*) records do not count as foreign.

checks.description: Detect scheduler methods that are large enough to be policy logic rather than dispatch and whose working state is a foreign engine's record. Parameter families are established from the compiler's own argument-type diagnostics on synthesized call sites against each detected method, so the foreign binding is structural, not name matching.
checks.detected_relation: oversized sc method (>= 24 statements) -> foreign engine record parameter (siplan*/si*, swmanager*)
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The maintenance scheduler is supposed to coordinate engines through their public interfaces and own only task selection, ordering and worker admission. When a scheduler method carries entire foreign maintenance policies and is handed the foreign engine's own records as working state, the scheduling class absorbs responsibilities that change for different reasons: matching conditions over index node internals, statistics computed from index headers, and log file lifecycle rules. Size without the foreign binding is ordinary local composition; the combination marks the responsibility cascade.

matches.evidence: Scheduler method implements the index engine's complete maintenance-plan cascade inline: a six-way switch over index plan types peeking the index rank-queue, per-node matching conditions (LSN bounds, cache-per-node watermark, duplicated-key ratio, expire timestamps, backup bounds, delayed node-gc list), locked-node retry handling, node locking and the backup-end fallback. The index component's dispatch and peek procedures were removed at the same time; the trace renderer for plans was re-homed beside it (E4). It takes the per-database scheduling record as the carrier for the foreign index record (db->index dereferenced inside).

Scheduler method computes a database statistics snapshot by walking the index rb-tree under the index lock, reading node header fields (stored and in-memory keys, duplicated keys, index size helpers, page counts) and index read counters, after copying scheduler state under the scheduler's own mutex. The statistics are accumulated into a scheduler-side record that was redefined to describe index internals (E5), replacing the index component's statistics module and record type, which were removed entirely.

Scheduler method owns the write-ahead-log maintenance policy: for rotation it reads the active log file's garbage-collection state under the log manager's spinlock and decides against the rotation watermark whether a new file is opened; for garbage collection it sweeps the manager's file list under the same spinlock and unlinks completed files through wal's wreckage primitive. The manager's own rotation-readiness decision was removed from wal, while the rotate and gc commands it still serves for external callers remain there, leaving one maintenance rule split across two components.

excluded.reason: 70 statements, but its interface binds only scheduler records (sc*, sctask*): scheduler-local task selection and periodic scheduling, not an absorbed foreign responsibility.
37 statements, interface binds only scheduler records (sc*, scworker*): per-worker step composition.
34 statements, interface binds only scheduler records (sc*, scdb*, sctask*, scworker*): backup procedure, already scheduling-local.
29 statements, interface binds only scheduler and runtime records (sc*, scdb*, scworker*, sr*): backup completion procedure.

22 statements, below the size clause (threshold 23). Although it binds a transaction log record, the committing step is scheduling work; thin interface use at this size is coordination, not an absorbed policy.
19 statements, below the size clause; constructor wiring to the work manager and log manager is initialization coordination.
20 statements, below the size clause: single-purpose plan rendering re-homed beside the absorbed cascade (E4). Credited as part of entry E1's cluster, not as an independent policy match.
5 statements; admission wrapper keeping per-queue worker limits in the scheduler (genuinely scheduler-local responsibility), delegating the maintenance decision outward.
